entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, and no inputs (the Cut names none). The vision is for invoicer maintainers, who build for the accountant (prints a client invoice from the spreadsheet at that client tax rate) and the installer (sets up the command on the accountant machine). The one change since done_at is the show-the-rate clause joining Nothing wrong prints.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
The job, from the Cut decision on the job: invoicer gives the accountant a command that prints a client invoice from the spreadsheet invoice lines at that client tax rate.
Roles named by the part of the job they come for: accountant, one who prints a client invoice; installer, one who sets up the command.
The accountant job gets done only if a developer installs Python and invoicer on the machine (Cut decision on who sets it up), so the installer is a role.
No person job left unclear: the Cut decision on the roles settles both; nothing to ask.
No split: every accountant counts a correct printed invoice as the job done; every installer a machine where the command runs.
No merge: accountant and installer count different results as their job done.
Two roles, so neither is named user.
O1 and O2 taken from the Cut decisions on the objectives, each one sentence with the role as subject.
Asked why: printing matters because the client gets a correct invoice at their rate; setup matters because the machine is ready with no further help. Both are ends in the role own work.
Two distinct ends: an installer can ready a machine without any invoice sent, and the reverse, so one objective each.
Tasks from the Cut decision on the task: O1 from spreadsheet lines and the client tax rate to the printed invoice; O2 from a machine with nothing of invoicer to the accountant running the command.
KR1.1 and KR2.1 measure how well as the failing share (help needed or wrong total; command not running after setup), per the Cut decision on key results.
KR1.2 and KR2.2 measure how fast as the time from task start to result, the role own time included.
Each key result has Lower is better.
Within each objective KR1 ranks before KR2, stated once in the template ranking line; no order across objectives.
No targets, by the template line on Goodhart law.
Pieces of work from the Cut: the invoice command, the README part for the accountant, the README setup section.
The command and the README accountant part serve O1; the README setup section serves O2.
O1 and O2 stay apart: the setup section serves O2 without O1, the README accountant part O1 without O2.
No piece names more than one objective, so none to split.
Every piece serves an objective; nothing to ask.
The one way and the ideas come from the person, as the Cut decisions on the one way and the ideas give them, the show-the-rate idea in the person own words; nothing to ask.
One way kept as one sentence of what the accountant sees: the command prints the finished invoice from the spreadsheet invoice lines plus the client tax rate.
Each idea with what it gives toward O1; Nothing wrong prints now also gives the client tax rate on the tax line, such as Tax (7%) 7.00 EUR, to catch a mistyped rate before the invoice goes out.
Moments from the Cut: installer sets up and sees it run; accountant gives lines and rate; invoice prints with the rate on its tax line, or a message says what to fix and the accountant runs again.

Each moment has an idea: setup by sheet as it is and rate each time (nothing to configure); giving lines by sheet as it is; printing by Nothing wrong prints, which now covers a readable but mistyped rate.
No idea proposed by me; the show-the-rate idea is the person own, so nothing to ask.
Three ideas kept, the template maximum; show-the-rate joins Nothing wrong prints, which it serves, per the Cut, rather than a fourth idea.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end. Roles names who it serves; Objectives and key results what each achieves and how it is measured; Concept the one way and its ideas.
Readers from the Cut name: invoicer maintainers, who decide what to build, and the accounting team, who check the vision says what they need.

Maintainers know Python and invoicer, and come to learn whom the command serves and which way to lean; the accounting team knows its spreadsheet and invoices, and comes to see its work described right.
The template three sections each hold one topic; no split.
Each role, objective, key result and idea is an item with its own ID or name; the template headings stay.
Roles and ideas are items in no order, so bulleted; key results nest under their objective; the ranking and no-target lines are an argument, so prose.
Readers words from the person answers in the Cut: invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, tax line, Tax (7%) 7.00 EUR.
Words chosen by the Cut decision on names; tax line taken from the person words for the invoice line that shows the tax; nothing coined to define.
Facts stated twice: the installer sets up none appears under two ideas, each for its own reason; no fact stated twice the same way.
Each fact keeps its place: the rate on the tax line under Nothing wrong prints, the rate given each time under its own idea.
No two places state a fact differently; nothing to ask.

Names grouped: invoicer, invoicer command, accountant, installer, accountant machine, the client tax rate, invoice line, spreadsheet, tax line; a mistyped rate would be a second name for the client tax rate.
Keep the client tax rate for the rate throughout, per the Cut decision on names, and write the new clause with it, not a mistyped rate.
No name refers to two things: invoice line (a spreadsheet line) and tax line (a line of the printed invoice) stay distinct.

Every Cut decision taken as it stands; the one change is the show-the-rate clause joining Nothing wrong prints. Settled without asking: the ranking line reads KR1.1 and KR2.1 come first, fixing the verb agreement. Nothing to ask.
With invoicer taken out, O1 reads the accountant sends each client a correct invoice, and O2 the installer gets a machine ready: ends, not features.
Each sentence asked whether it would change with the insides alone; the new tax line clause is what the accountant sees on the printed invoice, so it stays; no runtime is named.

E2E records: KR1.1 each printed invoice marked helped or wrong total; KR1.2 the times the spreadsheet opens and the invoice prints; KR2.1 each setup marked command not running; KR2.2 the setup start and first run times.
Choice no line names, decided by the ideas: whether to ask the accountant to confirm the rate before printing. Nothing wrong prints decides it: show the rate on the tax line, no extra prompt.
Headings are the template reference headings, Roles, Objectives and key results, Concept; kept.
The first line under each heading is the template own: the first role, the first objective, the one way; each says what the section gives.
Read headings and first lines for the maintainer and accounting team purposes; each leads to the section it needs.
Each sentence has a reader: maintainers and the accounting team need each role, objective, key result and idea; none marked.
No sentence marked, so no other document sought.
No sentence to move within the deliverable.
No sentence to move outside it; nothing to ask.
No sentence cut.
Words checked in the new clause; each carries a point the accountant needs.
Articles and small structure words kept.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as each reader; nothing a purpose needs is missing.
The tax line clause comes after the client tax rate is introduced in Roles, O1 and the one way.
Nothing depends on an outside page; the tax line example is stated in place.
The new clause starts from the client tax rate, already known, and ends with the new point, catching a mistype before sending.
No conditional instruction in the vision.
The exception to ranking, no order across objectives, is carried by the line that key results show their own objective, right after the rule.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end from the top; no place needed a look back or ahead.
Passages kept in the forms chosen: bulleted roles and ideas, nested key results, prose ranking line.
No sequence diagram needed; the moments of use stay in the ideas.
No structure diagram needed; the vision describes no parts.
The idea line holds one point for the template one short sentence: what the accountant gets instead of a wrong invoice, the rate on the tax line its second half.
The accountant is the subject with active verbs gets, sees, catch.
Pronouns checked: they is the accountant, one is the client tax rate, each within five words of a single fitting noun.
No noun made from a verb left to turn back.
Objects stay next to their verbs.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as a translator would; the ranking line verb fixed to come for its plural subject.
Words match the chosen ones; tax line in its usual meaning.
No coined term to define.
Abbreviations: O and KR are the template IDs under Objectives and key results; EUR is in the person example as it prints.
Each fact stated in full at its one place.
No repeated fact to replace with a link.
Kept names written the same throughout, with accountant, installer and invoicer in code format; the new clause uses the client tax rate.

docs/product-vision.md made: Nothing wrong prints now says the accountant sees the client tax rate on the tax line, such as Tax (7%) 7.00 EUR, to catch a mistype before the invoice goes out; the ranking line verb agrees; all else as signed off.

Tried in a throwaway copy as a maintainer reads it: no template comment or placeholder left, three ideas each for O1, the vision reads whole with the tax line clause in Nothing wrong prints; exit 0, nothing to mend.
Made written with each of the 13 Cut decisions placed, no More kept, and two points settled with their ground: the show-the-rate clause wording and the ranking line verb.

The check asked the ranking line to keep the template form and the Nothing wrong prints line to stay within 20 words a sentence: the ranking line is back to the template verb, the tax line clause is its own sentence, and the Made says so.
